evidence.title: US junk and corporate bond spreads surge in sign of market fears
evidence.summary: This article from August 2024 reports a significant surge in US junk and corporate bond spreads, including the ICE/BofA U.S. Investment Grade Corporate Bond Index spread. While not specifically Baa, it indicates a broader market trend of widening spreads due to market fears, which could influence Baa spreads. JPMorgan analysts' revised forecast for high-yield bond spreads to widen to 500 bp suggests a mechanism for spread widening.

evidence.title: A Tale of Two Job Reports - Moody's CRE
evidence.summary: This Moody's article from November 2024 discusses the bond market's reaction to economic data, specifically the 10-year Treasury yield. It notes that bond yields trended higher since September due to stronger-than-expected economic data and concerns about fiscal sustainability. Higher Treasury yields can impact the spread calculation, potentially leading to a narrowing if corporate bond yields don't rise as much, or a widening if they do.

evidence.title: US high-yield credit set for best returns in eight years in 2024
evidence.summary: This December 2024 article highlights strong performance in high-yield bonds in 2024, driven by corporate profitability and a soft economic landing. While focusing on high-yield, it mentions 'record-tight spreads in corporate bond markets' and a bullish outlook on US fixed income due to political factors. This suggests a countervailing factor to spread widening, as tighter spreads in the broader corporate bond market could influence Baa spreads.

evidence.title: Footnotes & Flashbacks: Asset Returns 12-8-24
evidence.summary: This December 2024 analysis mentions that 'HY OAS tightened by -72 bps YTD and IG -23 bps YTD.' This indicates a general trend of tightening spreads in both high-yield (HY) and investment-grade (IG) credit markets throughout 2024. This tightening trend acts as a countervailing factor against a significant widening of the Baa spread.
